newsitem.title: INDIA: India call eases despite SBI strike.
newsitem.headline: India call eases despite SBI strike.

text.p: An unofficial strike by the Bombay staff of the State Bank of India (SBI), India's leading bank, had only minimal impact on the call money market on Friday, dealers said.
Call rates did not flare up largely because of the inflow of about 39.0 billion rupees into the banking system from repurchase of repo securities, dealers said.
Call rates closed Friday at 5.50-6.50 percent compared to the opening level of7.50-8.50 percent.
Call briefly touched double-digits on Thursday before easing to close at 9.0-9.5 percent.
"RBI's repeated dollar buying is also adding to the liquidity," said a dealer at a state-run bank in Bombay.
SBI's foreign exchange operations were unaffected as the strike has not spread beyond Bombay.

SBI's staff in Bombay are striking for the second successive day to protest against suspension of some of their officers who handled accounts of CRB Capital Markets, a finance company now facing liquidation proceedings.
At Thursday's repo auction, RBI raised only 9.0 billion rupees against 48.0 billion at the previous auction.
"If there was no strike, they could have raised about 30.0 billion," a dealer at a lending institution said.
Some dealers expect the strike to be called off on Saturday which would exert further downward pressure on call rates.
